To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new sensor system was developed and tested to identify melanoma in the skin.

a) a sensor array can be used for the identification of the disease; and b) it has been possible to discriminate between healthy and melanoma‐affected subjects with a sensitivity and specificity of 100% using a gas sensor array in combination with the multivariate statistical analysis.

a) the volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emitted by human skin are different in melanoma‐affected subjects compared to healthy subjects and b) the differences can be used to identify melanoma with a sensor array, which is the first application in the field of cancer diagnosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of cancer‐affected skin tissues through the measurement and analysis of the volatile chemicals emitted from them.
the study of volatile compounds emitted from human skin and with the possibility to use them as markers of the presence of melanoma.
the possibility to detect cancer cells by measuring the chemical composition of their environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of sensor arrays is still in a preliminary phase, with a number of promising results but also a number of unsolved problems.
the identification of the volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emitted by the body could be a promising tool for the early diagnosis of cancer.
the use of gas sensors arrays for the identification of the presence of a cancer is still a matter of investigation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed an electronic nose for the identification and classification of the melanoma‐affected subjects.
the chemical composition of melanoma is different from healthy skin.
we are developing an array‐based system for the identification of cancer‐affected subjects by means of their exhaled breath composition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a gas sensor array can be successfully applied to the detection of melanoma.
the use of an artificial sensor array is able to detect the presence of melanoma with high sensitivity.
a gas sensor array is a promising tool to detect cancer in its early stage.
